name: Andronicus
charge: Murder of Onias the high priest under a sworn assurance
summary: Andronicus was left in authority as the king’s deputy, and Menelaus had given him some of the gold vessels stolen out of the temple. When Onias reproved the theft and took sanctuary at Daphne, Menelaus took Andronicus apart and prayed him to get the high priest into his hands; he came in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths, drew him out of the sanctuary though he was suspected, and shut him up without regard of justice. The king stripped him of his purple, led him through the whole city to the place of the murder, and slew him there.
offenseFull: Antiochus went in haste to settle a rising in Tarsus and Mallos and left Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy (2 Maccabees 4:30-31). Menelaus, having stolen certain vessels of gold out of the temple, gave some of them to Andronicus and sold others into Tyre and the cities round about; and when Onias knew the theft of a surety he reproved him and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne beside Antioch (2 Maccabees 4:32-33). The class showed on the map how far the high priest of Israel had to flee to be safe, out of Jerusalem and up into Syria, which is exactly what the wise man said a backbiting tongue does: it has disquieted many and driven them from nation to nation, pulled down strong cities and overthrown the houses of great men (Ecclesiasticus 28:13-15).

Menelaus then took Andronicus apart and prayed him to get Onias into his hands. He came to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths, and though he was suspected by him, persuaded him to come forth of the sanctuary, and shut him up immediately without regard of justice (2 Maccabees 4:34). He killed the true high priest, the man whose godliness had kept the city in peace (2 Maccabees 3:1), the man seen afterward in the vision holding up his hands and praying for the whole body of the Jews, virtuous and good, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue (2 Maccabees 15:12-14). Not only the Jews but many also of other nations took great indignation and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man (2 Maccabees 4:35), because Onias had a good report even among the nations. The class draws the standard for office out of that: a man must have a good report of them which are without (1 Timothy 3:7), walk honestly toward them that are without (1 Thessalonians 4:12), walk in wisdom toward them (Colossians 4:5), and keep his conversation honest among the Gentiles, so that they who speak against him as an evildoer may see his good works (1 Peter 2:12). Onias had that report without ever joining himself to them.
judgmentFull: When the king came back and heard the complaint he was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger he took away the purple from Andronicus, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city to that very place where he had committed the impiety against Onias, and there slew the cursed murderer (2 Maccabees 4:37-38).

The record calls that the Lord rewarding him his punishment as he had deserved. The class set the plain sayings beside it. For the work of a man shall he render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways (Job 34:11). He that does wrong shall receive for the wrong which he has done, and there is no respect of persons (Colossians 3:25). God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that shall he also reap; it might not be this year, and it might be next year, but it is coming (Galatians 6:7). The oath and the offered right hand were what drew the victim out of safety, and they did not cover the man who gave them. The king who had been served by the murder was the one who carried out the sentence, and he carried it out on the spot where the murder was done.

lawsResolved.text: If a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him with guile, he shall die.
You shall make no false or deceitful oath or covenant.
You shall not swear by God's name falsely.
God will judge and punish false swearers.
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.

text.text: While those things were in doing, they of Tarsus and Mallos made insurrection, because they were given to the king’s concubine, called Antiochus.
Then came the king in all haste to appease matters, leaving Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy.

Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about.
Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lieth by Antiochia.
Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.
A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.
A backbiting tongue hath cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labours.

Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed, him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded thereunto, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice.
Now when the holy city was inhabited with all peace, and the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness,

And this was his vision: That Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken also, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue, holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews.
This done, in like manner there appeared a man with gray hairs, and exceeding glorious, who was of a wonderful and excellent majesty.
Then Onias answered, saying, This is a lover of the brethren, who prayeth much for the people, and for the holy city, to wit, Jeremias the prophet of God.
For the which cause not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man.
Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.
Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.
Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.
Therefore Antiochus was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead.

And being kindled with anger, forthwith he took away Andronicus his purple, and rent off his clothes, and leading him through the whole city unto that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.
Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.
Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.
